newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slump, nervousness continues.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slump, nervousness continues.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished much lower again Monday as the sour sentiment of last week continued to hammer the market.
Traders reported that there was more foreign selling and with key U.S. indicators due for release later this week, nervousness was seen continuing.
"Basically the market fell on (Federal Reserve Chairman) Alan Greenspan, but nobody knows how U.S. treasuries will trade and the local market will continue to trade off them," said a trader.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.86 to 125.49.
"The market will continue to be volatile in coming days," said another trader.
According to players the second leg of Greenspan's annual testimony to Congress on Wednesday and the release of U.S. unemployment figures on Friday are set to maintain investor wariness.
"There exists the belief in the market that the spread to U.S. Treasuries will continue to widen," said the first trader.
Call money rates rose to 5.75 percent from 5.38 percent.
